claims.claim: The 24 February 2026 announcement counts 795 Mexican fintech startups and compares that with an adjusted 781 in its prior baseline.
claims.uncertainty: A publisher-defined sector population, not a list of every Mexican startup or this batch denominator. Full company roster not extracted.

claims.claim: Endeavor reports a map of 153 technology startups founded in Monterrey since 2015 and a separate founder survey of 49 respondents. Its analysis emphasises corporate procurement and access-to-capital friction.
claims.uncertainty: Mapping universe and survey sample differ; neither is a national denominator. Main article is dated 2026-09-28 while index/search dates differ. Linked DocSend report was not accessed.

claims.claim: incMTY convened academic institutions, government, investors and technology founders in Monterrey in March 2026.
claims.uncertainty: Historical event; not an application window or startup investment.

claims.claim: Tec described a hub in the Monterrey Innovation District connecting applied research, scientific ventures and industry, with laboratories and startup spaces.
claims.uncertainty: Article dated 25 May announced opening on 26 May 2026; facilities and participation do not establish investment.

claims.claim: Government programme for technology ventures; listed requirements include at least two team members and direct or indirect impact in Zapopan. It lists mentoring, business training, networking and possible evaluated financing.
claims.uncertainty: The accessed listing gives 6 June 2026 deadline. Search snippets elsewhere give 20 June; not reconciled and not promoted as currently open.

claims.claim: NAFIN describes a trust investing in private capital funds with impact in Mexico and explicitly says it currently has no resources to commit.
claims.uncertainty: Fund-manager vehicle, not a currently available direct startup grant; undated status requires recheck before recommendations.

claims.claim: NAFIN describes CMIC as a federal fund-of-funds vehicle, with Nafin, Bancomext, Banobras and Focir as institutional shareholders.
claims.uncertainty: Legacy page contains dated wording. Used for institutional architecture only; current product availability not verified.

claims.claim: AMEXCAP represents private capital managers and describes venture capital as one of six strategies alongside growth, private credit, real estate, infrastructure/energy and family offices.
claims.uncertainty: Its 2025 VC figure differs slightly from later secondary reports. No national investment total is normalised or aggregated in this packet.

claims.claim: Luchadores funds supply a Latin American venture network and portfolio discovery source. Visible Mexico labels include Conekta, Clip, Jüsto, Deporprivé, Flat, Baubap, Graviti and Plerk.
claims.uncertainty: Page repeats carousel names and exposes 15 pagination controls. Neither pagination exhaustion nor a complete Mexican portfolio was established. Footer says figures are as of 30 September 2022. Membership is not round participation.

claims.claim: Angel Ventures describes its investor network, angel education and investment-support activities, including a Guadalajara network active since 2014.
claims.uncertainty: Undated page contains 2018/2019-era metrics; current member counts and transaction totals are not reused.

claims.claim: Dalus describes investments in Latin American startups from seed through Series A and B.
claims.uncertainty: Dollar-symbol ticket-size text is not normalised to USD. Portfolio page is mostly dynamic images; no exhaustive roster.

claims.claim: Wollef explicitly targets pre-seed, seed and Series A; its visible portfolio examples span fintech, commerce, SaaS and marketplaces.
claims.uncertainty: Partnered years are not financing dates. Selected company examples are discovery leads; no portfolio-to-round inference.

claims.claim: DILA targets Spanish-speaking founders doing business in Latin America and US companies serving Hispanic markets; the official page lists Mexico City and Miami offices.
claims.uncertainty: Office geography is not fund incorporation. Portfolio totals are not a Mexico startup denominator.

claims.claim: Startup México describes a three-month acceleration programme, mentoring, investor pitching and digital/commercial strategy; its stated entry profile includes businesses with annual sales above MXN500,000 and individuals with at least two years of business operations.
claims.uncertainty: Published eligibility description only; application availability, pricing and deadlines were not established; not represented as free or currently open.
